input_signals.name: HealthScoredProfitability
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), SUMRANK(RATIO(re, at), RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: High profitability is most valuable when it sits on a foundation of accumulated retained earnings and liquid working-capital solvency, since such firms can self-fund and survive shocks, making current profits persistent.
input_signals.reasoning: The profitability rank (Theme A) is scaled by a two-channel balance-sheet health score combining retained-earnings depth and net-working-capital coverage of total liabilities (Theme B), so profits are credited only when the firm is financially sound. Young, deficit-laden or illiquid firms with temporarily high margins get pushed down, isolating durable operating strength. The multiplicative structure makes the quality score a modulator of the profitability payoff rather than an additive competitor.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oibdp, at ), 3 ) ), sumrank( ratio( re, at ), ratio( sub( act, lct ), lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: AdditiveHealthProfit
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3), SUMRANK(RATIO(re, at), RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Profitability and balance-sheet health both carry independent premia, and an additive rank combination should span more of the cross-section (avoiding the rank-product compression that pushes moderate firms to the middle) while retaining the same economic story.
input_signals.reasoning: This deliberately isolates one design choice relative to the archive winner: the same three channels (smoothed EBITDA/assets, retained-earnings depth, net working capital over total liabilities) combined additively rather than multiplicatively. If the multiplicative form's alpha was limited by extreme-rank concentration and unstable long/short membership, the additive version should raise ls_talpha and Sharpe; if instead the conditioning is essential, the additive version will weaken, which is itself informative.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ma( ratio( oibdp, at ), 3 ), sumrank( ratio( re, at ), ratio( sub( act, lct ), lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: DebtServicedProfitSpread
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(oiadp, xint), at), WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, ADD(dltt, dlc)), 2))
input_signals.hypothesis: Profitability that survives the cost of debt service and that comfortably covers the outstanding debt stock is durable operating strength, whereas equally high pre-interest profitability on a heavily indebted balance sheet is transient and largely a claim of creditors.
input_signals.reasoning: The first channel is operating profit net of interest expense scaled by assets (profitability theme), the second is EBITDA coverage of total debt (quality theme via dltt and dlc), so leverage enters through earnings capacity rather than as a raw balance-sheet ratio. Firms with negative EBITDA automatically receive a low coverage rank, so the interaction does not invert for distressed names. This tests debt-service capacity as the quality modulator, a channel absent from the archive.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( sub( oiadp, xint ), at ), winsor( ratio( oibdp, add( dltt, dlc ) ), 2 ) )

input_signals.name: ProfitToLiabilities
input_signals.expression: IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oiadp, xint), lt), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Operating profit after interest measured against the total stock of obligations is the cleanest single statement of the interaction: the same dollar of profit is worth more when fewer creditor claims stand against it.
input_signals.reasoning: The numerator is a profitability flow net of financing cost (oiadp, xint) and the denominator is total liabilities (lt, quality-exclusive), so leverage and profitability are fused into one economically interpretable coverage ratio rather than two ranked channels. Industry z-scoring removes structural differences in capital intensity and leverage norms, and the parsimony should deliver higher coverage and a more stable long-short membership than the three-channel composites. It is the natural minimal test of whether the archive's composite alphas come from the profitability-per-obligation channel itself.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( oiadp, xint ), lt ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: ConsolidatedDurableProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), SUMRANK(WINSOR(RATIO(oibdp, ADD(dltt, dlc)), 2), RATIO(re, at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The two channels that independently generated alpha — debt-service capacity and retained-earnings depth — should reinforce each other, because a firm that can both cover its debt from current earnings and has historically retained profits has proven durable operating strength.
input_signals.reasoning: It keeps the multiplicative conditioning structure that produced the archive's best FF5 alpha but replaces the weak net-working-capital channel with the stronger EBITDA-to-debt coverage channel from DebtServicedProfitSpread. This is a deliberate consolidation test: if alpha and t-alpha both rise relative to HealthScoredProfitability, the quality modulator is solvency rather than liquidity.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oibdp, at ), 3 ) ), sumrank( winsor( ratio( oibdp, add( dltt, dlc ) ), 2 ), ratio( re, at ) ) )

input_signals.name: MaturityBackedProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, ADD(dltt, dlc)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: High profitability is more valuable when the debt financing it is long-dated; a heavy share of current debt exposes profitable firms to rollover and refinancing shocks that truncate the value of their earnings stream.
input_signals.reasoning: The quality modulator is debt maturity structure — the share of short-term debt in total debt (dlc, dltt) — a financial-health dimension untested in the archive and distinct from leverage level, coverage, or retained earnings. Multiplying industry ranks conditions the profitability premium on refinancing safety, so profitable firms funded with commercial paper are pushed toward the middle while equally profitable term-funded firms rise.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oibdp, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( dlc, add( dltt, dlc ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: SmoothedHealthProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(re, at), 3), MA(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The durable-profitability premium is real but its portfolio implementation is noisy because the health channels are measured from single-year balance sheets; smoothing them should hold the same firms in the extreme buckets longer and raise the reliability of the abnormal return.
input_signals.reasoning: This isolates exactly one design choice against the archive's best signal: three-year averaging of the retained-earnings and net-working-capital channels, leaving the economic content and the multiplicative conditioning untouched. If ls_talpha and Sharpe rise while alpha holds near 2-3%, the limiting factor was measurement noise and portfolio turnover rather than the mechanism.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oibdp, at ), 3 ) ), sumrank( ma( ratio( re, at ), 3 ), ma( ratio( sub( act, lct ), lt ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: NearTermCoverageProfit
input_signals.expression: IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(oiadp, lct), 1))
input_signals.hypothesis: Operating profit measured against *current* liabilities captures the economically binding constraint — whether this year's earnings cover this year's claims — and should be a sharper, faster-moving interaction than profit over total liabilities.
input_signals.reasoning: This isolates the denominator choice against ProfitToLiabilities, which delivered a respectable alpha t-stat but a zero Sharpe because total liabilities move too slowly to differentiate firms in real time. Current liabilities (lct) refresh annually with operating conditions, so the ratio should reprice faster and produce a spread with positive stand-alone Sharpe as well as alpha.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( oiadp, lct ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: DistressScoredProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3)), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), at), RATIO(re, lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Profitability is most valuable in firms far from financial distress, where distance is measured Altman-style by working-capital cushion relative to the asset base and accumulated retained earnings relative to creditor claims.
input_signals.reasoning: It keeps the successful multiplicative form but re-normalizes both health channels in the distress-score convention (working capital over assets, retained earnings over liabilities) instead of the ad hoc scalings used in gen 0, making the modulator a genuine solvency-distance measure. Because the two channels are scaled by different bases, the composite carries information about both cushion size and creditor coverage rather than double-counting one denominator.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oiadp, at ), 3 ) ), sumrank( ratio( sub( act, lct ), at ), ratio( re, lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: CashDebtServiceProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, lt), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Operating cash flow relative to total liabilities is the creditor-relevant, cash-based measure of financial health; profitable firms whose cash flow comfortably services their obligations have durable operating strength, while accrual-based coverage ratios can be gamed.
input_signals.reasoning: Gen 2 showed accrual-based debt coverage (EBITDA/debt) weakened the multiplicative winner, so this tests whether the cash-based analogue — smoothed oancf over lt — is the version that carries information. It separates the "can the balance sheet be serviced from cash" channel from the liquidity-cushion and retention channels, so the result tells us which of the three solvency dimensions the alpha actually needs.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oibdp, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( ma( ratio( oancf, lt ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: DistressScoredProfitPlus
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3)), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), at), SUMRANK(RATIO(re, lt), MA(RATIO(oancf, lt), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Solvency distance is best measured on three complementary axes — liquid cushion, accumulated retention, and current cash-flow coverage of creditor claims — so adding smoothed cash-flow coverage to the leading distress score should make the durability filter more complete.
input_signals.reasoning: It extends the archive leader with the one health channel that independently showed the best cross-sectional slope and Sharpe (smoothed oancf/lt, fmb 2.68, Sharpe 0.22) while keeping the proven multiplicative conditioning and normalizations. If alpha and t-alpha both rise, the cash-coverage axis carries information orthogonal to the cushion and retention axes; if they fall, the distress score is already saturated and parsimony should be preferred.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oiadp, at ), 3 ) ), sumrank( ratio( sub( act, lct ), at ), sumrank( ratio( re, lt ), ma( ratio( oancf, lt ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: NetOfInterestDistressProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(oiadp, xint), at), 3)), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), at), RATIO(re, lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Charging interest expense against operating profit removes the part of reported profitability that belongs to creditors, so the profitability leg itself should discriminate levered from unlevered operating strength before the solvency modulator is applied.
input_signals.reasoning: This isolates a single design choice in the leader: the profitability numerator becomes profit after financing cost (oiadp − xint) instead of pre-interest operating profit. Because leverage then enters through both the flow and the balance sheet, the signal should sharpen the distinction between durable operating strength and levered profitability, which is exactly the task's economic story.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( sub( oiadp, xint ), at ), 3 ) ), sumrank( ratio( sub( act, lct ), at ), ratio( re, lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: RetentionCoveredProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3)), IND_RANK(RATIO(re, lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The durable-profitability premium comes primarily from accumulated retained earnings relative to creditor claims — the cleanest evidence that a firm's past profits were real and were kept inside the business — rather than from the short-term liquidity cushion.
input_signals.reasoning: This is a deliberate channel-attribution test: the leader's two health channels are stripped to retention coverage alone, holding the profitability leg and multiplicative structure fixed. If alpha and t-alpha are close to the leader's, the working-capital term is redundant and the parsimonious signal is preferable for stability; if they drop sharply, the cushion term is doing real work and future refinements should build on liquidity.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oiadp, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( re, lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: LeanOperatingProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), xsga), at), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(act, sale))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Durable profitability is generated by capital-light operations: firms that produce a dollar of sales with fewer current assets tied up in receivables and inventory convert profits into cash quickly, whereas equally profitable firms with bloated current assets are recognizing revenue before it is collected.
input_signals.reasoning: This tests working-capital *efficiency* (act/sale) as the quality modulator, which is economically the opposite of the winner's working-capital *cushion* term, so the result discriminates between the safety interpretation and the operating-quality interpretation of current assets. The profitability leg uses a clean operating margin built from revt, cogs, and xsga, keeping the two channels informationally distinct.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( sub( sub( revt, cogs ), xsga ), at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( act, sale ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: WeakestLinkDurableProfit
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3)), IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), at), RATIO(re, lt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Durable operating strength requires profitability and financial health simultaneously, so a firm should be scored by its weaker attribute; a product form still lets an extreme value on one axis compensate for mediocrity on the other, which blurs the long and short legs.
input_signals.reasoning: Using MIN on the two industry-ranked legs enforces strict conjunction: the long portfolio contains only firms that are high on both profitability and solvency distance, and the short portfolio contains any firm that fails on either axis. This is an operator-structure test of the same economics as the archive leader and could raise both t-alpha and Sharpe by producing more homogeneous, more slowly turning extreme buckets.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oiadp, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( sumrank( ratio( sub( act, lct ), at ), ratio( re, lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: CushionCoveredProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3)), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The durable-profitability premium is driven by the liquidity cushion: profitable firms holding large net working capital can fund operations and withstand shocks internally, so their current earnings persist, whereas equally profitable firms with no cushion must refinance to survive.
input_signals.reasoning: This is the mirror-image attribution test to RetentionCoveredProfit, which stripped the leader down to retention and failed; here the leader is stripped down to the cushion channel with the profitability leg and multiplicative form held fixed. If alpha stays near the leader's 3.5-4%, the cushion is the sole active modulator and later refinements should build exclusively on liquidity.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oiadp, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( sub( act, lct ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: TripleConjunctionProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(oiadp, xint), at), 3)), MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(re, lt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Durability requires profitability, liquidity, and a retention record jointly; a signal that multiplies all three ranks forms a long leg of firms that satisfy every condition, which should be a cleaner portfolio than one where a high sum of two health ranks can offset a weak third.
input_signals.reasoning: The leader averages the two health ranks before conditioning, letting retention substitute for liquidity; the triple product enforces conjunction and tests whether the weak stand-alone retention channel nevertheless adds value as a *filter* rather than as an additive score. Comparing it against Signal 1 tells us whether retention has any incremental role once the cushion is present.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( sub( oiadp, xint ), at ), 3 ) ), mul( ind_rank( ratio( sub( act, lct ), at ) ), ind_rank( ratio( re, lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: TurnaroundProfitability
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(re, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Among firms with accumulated deficits, current operating profitability is a genuine turnaround signal that the market is slow to price: past losses depressed expectations, so newly demonstrated profitability delivers positive abnormal returns.
input_signals.reasoning: DeficitProfitTrap generated the archive's largest alpha and Sharpe with the sign opposite to my prior, but its construction assigned zero to all non-deficit firms, so the spread may have been an artifact of that zero mass forming the short leg. Replacing the indicator with a continuous rank of *negative* retained earnings tests the same economics with a properly distributed signal, and its result determines whether the retention channel enters the final signal with a positive or negative sign.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oibdp, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( re, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: EarningsCoverageDistressProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(oiadp, xint), at), 3)), SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), at), SUMRANK(RATIO(re, lt), RATIO(oibdp, lt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The gain from adding a third coverage channel to the distress score reflects creditor-claim coverage in general, not cash-flow data specifically, so an earnings-based coverage term should reproduce the improvement without the sample loss from cash-flow reporting.
input_signals.reasoning: DistressScoredProfitPlus achieved the highest alpha (4.2%) and Sharpe (0.33) but its oancf channel cut coverage from 0.12 to 0.079, raising the risk that the improvement is a sample-composition artifact. Substituting EBITDA-to-liabilities restores full coverage while keeping the three-axis solvency structure and the net-of-interest profitability leg, giving a direct test of whether the extra alpha is economic or sample-driven.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( sub( oiadp, xint ), at ), 3 ) ), sumrank( ratio( sub( act, lct ), at ), sumrank( ratio( re, lt ), ratio( oibdp, lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: SupplierFinancedProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3)), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(lt, ADD(dltt, dlc)), lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Profitability financed by non-interest-bearing operating liabilities — payables, accruals, deferred items — is higher quality than profitability financed by debt, because such funding is interest-free, self-renewing with operations, and evidences bargaining power over suppliers.
input_signals.reasoning: This introduces liability *composition* rather than liability level, cushion, or maturity as the quality modulator, an axis untested in the archive and economically distinct from all prior channels. It also gives an alternative reading of why cushion measures work: if operating-liability financing is what matters, this signal should carry comparable alpha with different portfolio composition.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oiadp, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( sub( lt, add( dltt, dlc ) ), lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: SmoothedTripleConjunction
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(oiadp, xint), at), 3)), MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), at), 3)), IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(re, lt), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The three-way durability conjunction is economically correct but measured with single-year balance-sheet noise; averaging the liquidity cushion and retention coverage over three years should hold the same firms in the extreme buckets and raise the reliability of the abnormal return.
input_signals.reasoning: This isolates one design choice against the archive leader — three-year smoothing of both quality legs — leaving the economics and the conjunctive structure untouched. If t-alpha and Sharpe rise with alpha intact, residual noise in annual balance-sheet items was the binding constraint on portfolio evidence.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( sub( oiadp, xint ), at ), 3 ) ), mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( sub( act, lct ), at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( ma( ratio( re, lt ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: CashCoveredQuadConjunction
input_signals.expression: MUL(MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(oiadp, xint), at), 3)), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), at))), MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(re, lt)), IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, lt), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cash-flow coverage of creditor claims is a fourth, non-redundant durability condition: a firm can be profitable, liquid, and historically retentive yet still fail to generate cash against its obligations.
input_signals.reasoning: Adding smoothed oancf/lt as a fourth multiplicative filter tests whether the highest-alpha, highest-Sharpe result in the archive (DistressScoredProfitPlus, 4.2%, Sharpe 0.33) came from cash-coverage information or merely from the restricted cash-flow-reporting sample. Because the structure otherwise matches the leader exactly, a rise in alpha at similar t-alpha with coverage near 0.08 would indicate real cash information, while a flat result would confirm the sample-composition explanation.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( sub( oiadp, xint ), at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( sub( act, lct ), at ) ) ), mul( ind_rank( ratio( re, lt ) ), ind_rank( ma( ratio( oancf, lt ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: LiquidAssetShareProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3)), IND_RANK(RATIO(act, at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: What makes profitability durable may be asset-side liquidity — the share of the asset base held in cash, receivables and inventory that can be redeployed or liquidated — rather than the netting of current liabilities against it.
input_signals.reasoning: CushionCoveredProfit and LeanOperatingProfit jointly imply that current assets enter positively, but both confound asset liquidity with current-liability structure; this strips the modulator to the pure asset-composition ratio act/at. If it matches the cushion version's t-alpha, the mechanism is asset liquidity and future signals should drop the lct term, simplifying the construct and improving coverage.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oiadp, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( act, at ) ) )

input_signals.name: ClaimsCoveredTriple
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(oiadp, xint), at), 3)), MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(act, lt)), IND_RANK(RATIO(re, lt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Liquid resources should be measured against *all* creditor claims rather than only current ones, because long-term debt eventually competes for the same liquid assets; profitability plus full-claim liquidity coverage is the sharpest statement of durable, unlevered operating strength.
input_signals.reasoning: This substitutes act/lt for the (act−lct)/at cushion inside the winning triple conjunction, making both quality legs denominated in total liabilities so the score is a coherent coverage-of-claims measure. Gen 5 showed the stricter net-liquid form (act−lt)/at delivered good alpha but a weak FMB slope, suggesting the subtraction, not the concept, hurt the cross-sectional fit; a ratio normalization should retain the alpha while restoring the slope.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( sub( oiadp, xint ), at ), 3 ) ), mul( ind_rank( ratio( act, lt ) ), ind_rank( ratio( re, lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: MarginConjunctionProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 3)), MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(re, lt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Durable operating strength may be better identified by pricing power in the income statement — the operating margin per dollar of sales — than by return on the asset base, since margin is less mechanically related to the balance-sheet quality legs it is combined with.
input_signals.reasoning: Every strong archive signal scales profit by assets, which shares its denominator with the cushion channel and can induce mechanical correlation between the legs; replacing it with a sales-based margin makes the profitability and quality legs informationally independent. This isolates the profitability-leg definition while holding the winning conjunction fixed, telling us whether the interaction is margin-driven or asset-turnover-driven.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oibdp, sale ), 3 ) ), mul( ind_rank( ratio( sub( act, lct ), at ) ), ind_rank( ratio( re, lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: DebtVersusLiquidityProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), act))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The relevant financial-health condition is how much interest-bearing debt stands against the firm's liquid resources; profitable firms whose debt is small relative to current assets face no refinancing constraint and their earnings stream is durable.
input_signals.reasoning: This is a new quality axis — debt scaled by liquid assets rather than by total assets or netted inside working capital — which failed as a level (leverage/assets) but should work if the operative mechanism is liquidity-adjusted refinancing risk, exactly what the cushion results hint at. It also uses only debt and current assets, so it is economically distinct from retention coverage and testable at full coverage.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oiadp, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( add( dltt, dlc ), act ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: LiquidTripleConjunction
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(oiadp, xint), at), 3)), MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(act, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(re, lt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Durable operating strength is profitability net of financing cost, earned on a liquid asset base, by a firm that has accumulated retained earnings against its creditor claims; asset liquidity is the cleaner measure of financial flexibility than net working capital because it does not net out routine trade financing.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the cushion leg of the archive leader with the act/at modulator that produced the best FMB slope and Sharpe in gen 6, holding the profitability leg and the retention filter fixed. If it beats TripleConjunctionProfit on t-alpha while keeping Sharpe near 0.3, it becomes the consolidated signal: same alpha magnitude, better cross-sectional slope and better stand-alone risk-adjusted spread.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( sub( oiadp, xint ), at ), 3 ) ), mul( ind_rank( ratio( act, at ) ), ind_rank( ratio( re, lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: QuadLiquidityRetentionProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(oiadp, xint), at), 3)), IND_RANK(RATIO(act, at))), MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(re, lt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Asset liquidity and the net working-capital cushion capture different things — how liquid the assets are versus how much of that liquidity is unencumbered by near-term claims — so requiring both alongside profitability and retention should isolate the most unambiguously durable firms.
